title: Storage-Elevation (Trapezoidal Integration)

S(h).description: Cumulative storage volume at elevation h

Ai.description: Reservoir surface area at elevation i

applicability: Prismoidal formula (more accurate): S = (Δh/3)(A1 + 4Am + A2) where Am = area at mid-elevation. Computed from topographic survey or DEM.
source: General surveying — USBR Design of Small Dams

title: Rippl Mass Curve — Required Storage
equation: S_required = max[Σ(Di - Ii)] for continuous periods where D > I

S_required.description: Minimum active storage to meet demand through critical drought

Ii.description: Inflow in period i (adjusted for evaporation and seepage losses)

applicability: Apply to longest available streamflow record. Must include worst known drought. For short records, extend with stochastic hydrology.

title: Sequent Peak Algorithm

St.description: Required storage at end of period t

Dt.description: Total demand plus losses in period t

applicability: S_required = max(St) over entire simulation. Initialize S0 = 0. Run through record twice to capture droughts spanning the end/start boundary. More robust than graphical mass curve for computer implementation.

title: Brune Trap Efficiency (Median Curve)
equation: TE ≈ 100 × [1 - (1 / (1 + Δ × C/I))]  where Δ ≈ 0.0021 (empirical fit)
alt_form: Read directly from Brune's (1953) graph: C/I = 0.01 → TE ≈ 60%; C/I = 0.10 → TE ≈ 87%; C/I = 1.0 → TE ≈ 97%

TE.description: Trap efficiency (% of incoming sediment retained)

γ_d.description: Dry bulk density of deposited sediment (1.0–1.5 t/m³ typical)

E_loss.description: Net evaporation volume loss from reservoir

A_res.description: Reservoir surface area at current pool level

title: Reservoir Water Balance
equation: ΔS = I + P_res - O - E_gross×A - Seepage

ΔS.description: Change in reservoir storage over time step

A.description: Average reservoir surface area during period

applicability: Fundamental accounting equation. Seepage is often computed as residual after measuring all other terms. Solved on monthly or daily time step.

title: Wind-Generated Wave Height (Significant Wave, SMB Method)
equation: Hs = 0.0016 × √(F) × U²/g  (simplified SMB for restricted fetch)

U.description: Wind speed over water (sustained, adjusted to over-water)

applicability: Used for freeboard determination and riprap sizing. Fetch limited by reservoir geometry. USACE Shore Protection Manual (now CEM) or USBR method.
